item.title: Izumo Soba: Dark Buckwheat Noodles in Stacked Bowls — Guide
item.description: Izumo soba is counted among the three great soba traditions of Japan, and it is distinctive from the first glance: because the whole buckwheat grain, husk included, is milled, the noodles are darker in colour, firmer, and much nuttier and more strongly flavoured than the pale soba of Tokyo. It is served in two classic styles. Warigo soba comes in a stack of three small round lacquer bowls, over which you pour the concentrated broth and condiments bowl by bowl.

item.title: Shimane Food Guide: Izumo Soba, Nodoguro & Lake Shinji Delicacies
item.description: Shimane’s food culture is built on cold water, deep lakes, and centuries of tea ceremony ritual. The prefecture produces some of the most celebrated ingredients in Japan — blackthroat seaperch that Tokyo fish markets pay premium prices for, tiny freshwater clams whose broth is claimed to cure hangovers and revive the weary, and a style of soba that requires a specific pouring technique most visitors get wrong on the first try.
